# **NFS 6 Hot Pursuit 2 file specs** #

*Last time updated: 2026-11-13 15:32:47.656826+00:00*

*Generated by [TailsLab](../README.md) from its parser code.*


# **Info by file extensions** #

**compNN.o**, **trackg.o**, **skyg.o**, **levelNN\levelG.o** track geometry. [EaglModel](#eaglmodel)

**tracks\<location\>\persist.viv** **skyg.o** + **sky.fsh** the location's sky (every levelNN of the location draws the same one): meshes around the camera (cloud cap, sky band, horizon ring, the sea below the horizon in Medit, Parkland and Tropics), drawn in render method order, alpha blended, 12.4 units below the eye (NFSHP2.exe, see `library/utils/nfs6_sky_to_spherical.py`). **Tr.ini** (`[strip]` horizon, `[clouds]`, `[sun]`...), **sun.ini** and **Fog.ini** are not read by NFSHP2.exe; **levelNN\lighting.ini** sets the sun glow (`[SunGlow]`), ambient and sun light, **levelNN\drvpath.ini** `[effectsN]` the fog of each compartment (the sky's fog density is FogSkyDensity * FogDensity * 0.04).

**cars\<car>\car.viv** car: **car.o** model (also **carRigid.o**, **carM.o** and **carRigidM.o** with left and right windows swapped, **shadow.o**, bones in **skeleton.o**: [EaglModel](#eaglmodel)), **car.fsh** wheel textures. [BigfBlock](#bigfblock)

**cars\<car>\skin.viv** car paint textures **skinNN.fsh**, their colors are in **vehicle.ini**. [BigfBlock](#bigfblock)

**levelNN\aipaths.dat** race route. [Nfs6AiPaths](#nfs6aipaths)

**cars\<car>\car.ini**, **car_hp.ini**, **car_cop.ini**, **carracer.ini** car physics (player, hot pursuit, police, AI racer). [Nfs6CarIni](#nfs6carini)

**cars\<car>\vehicle.ini** shading, skins, paint swatches, light glows. [Nfs6VehicleIni](#nfs6vehicleini)

**cars\<car>\bounds.ini** bounding boxes. [Nfs6BoundsIni](#nfs6boundsini)

**cars\<car>\geomdata.ini** levels of detail and damage zones of the model's geometries. [Nfs6GeomDataIni](#nfs6geomdataini)

**cars\<car>\damage.ini**, **lod.ini** (not read by the game). [Nfs6DamageIni](#nfs6damageini), [Nfs6LodIni](#nfs6lodini)

**cars\Cars.ini** the car list. [Nfs6CarsIni](#nfs6carsini)

**cars\Cameras.ini** race cameras. [Nfs6CamerasIni](#nfs6camerasini)

**cars\RearView.ini** (not read by the game). [Nfs6RearViewIni](#nfs6rearviewini)

**cars\reflection.ini** car reflections. [Nfs6ReflectionIni](#nfs6reflectionini)

**cars\cartable.viv** engine sound tables **engine.rpm**, **engine.ctb**, **engine.htb**, **engine.ltb**, **engine.btb**. [Nfs6EngineAudioTable](#nfs6engineaudiotable)

**audio/music/\*.asf** song (names in **music.ini**), **audio/speech/\<language\>/radio.viv** police radio speech (EA MicroTalk, not decoded). [EaAudioStreams](#eaaudiostreams)

**\*.BNK** sound bank. [EaSoundBank](#easoundbank)

**\*.FFN** bitmap font. [FfnFont](#ffnfont)

**\*.FSH** image archive. [ShpiBlock](#shpiblock)

**\*.VIV** archive with some data. [BigfBlock](#bigfblock)

Did not find what you need or some given data is wrong? Please submit an
[issue](https://github.com/AndyGura/nfs-resources-converter/issues/new)


# **Block specs** #
## **Archives** ##
### **ShpiBlock** ###
#### **Size**: 16..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: A container of images and palettes for them ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 4 | UTF-8 string. Always == "SHPI" | Resource ID |
| 4 | **length** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | The length of this SHPI block in bytes |
| 8 | **num_items** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | An amount of items |
| 12 | **shpi_dir** | 4 | UTF-8 string | One of: "LN32", "GIMX", "WRAP". The purpose is unknown |
| 16 | **items_descr** | num_items\*8 | Array of `num_items` items<br/>Item size: 8 bytes<br/>Item type: 8-bytes record, first 4 bytes is a UTF-8 string, last 4 bytes is an unsigned integer (little-endian) | An array of items, each of them represents name of SHPI item (image or palette) and offset to item data in file, relatively to SHPI block start (where resource id string is presented). Names are not always unique |
| 16 + num_items\*8 | **pre_items_payload** | up to the first item offset | Bytes | Bytes between the end of `items_descr` and the first item: padding, or data which no item offset points to |
| 16 + num_items\*8 + up to the first item offset | **data_bytes** | up to end of block | Bytes | A part of block, where items data is located. Offsets to some of the entries are defined in `items_descr` block. Between them there can be non-indexed entries (palettes and texts). Possible item types:<br/>- [EacImage](#eacimage)<br/>- [EacPalette](#eacpalette) |
### **BigfBlock** ###
#### **Size**: 16..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: A block-container with various data: image archives, GEO geometries, sound banks, other BIGF blocks... In the PSX TNFS car archives (`.VSM` / `.WSM`) every item ends with its own CRC footer, counted in the item length ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 4 | UTF-8 string. Always == "BIGF" | Resource ID |
| 4 | **length** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | The length of this BIGF block in bytes. NFS6 stores the length without padding between items: header plus item lengths |
| 8 | **num_items** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | An amount of items |
| 12 | **unk0** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Unknown purpose |
| 16 | **items_descr** | num_items\*9..? | Array of `num_items` items<br/>Item type: [BigfItemDescriptionBlock](#bigfitemdescriptionblock) | Descriptions of items: offset, length and name of each of them |
| 16 + num_items\*9..? | **pre_items_payload** | up to the first item offset | Bytes | Bytes between the end of `items_descr` and the first item: padding, or data which no item offset points to |
| 16 + num_items\*9 + up to the first item offset..? | **data_bytes** | up to end of block | Bytes | A part of block, where items data is located. Offsets and lengths are defined in previous block. Possible item types:<br/>- [ShpiBlock](#shpiblock), can be compressed like QFS file<br/>- [BigfBlock](#bigfblock)<br/>- [EaSoundBank](#easoundbank)<br/>- pure TGA image |
### **BigfItemDescriptionBlock** ###
#### **Size**: 9..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Description of a single item of BIGF archive ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **offset** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Offset of item data, relative to BIGF block start |
| 4 | **length** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Length of item data in bytes |
| 8 | **name** | 1..? | Null-terminated UTF-8 string. Ends with first occurrence of zero byte | Item name (file name). Used as file name when the archive is unpacked |
### **EaSoundBank** ###
#### **Size**: 12..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: EA sound bank "BNKl" (*.BNK of NFS2, NFS2 SE, NFS3, NFS4, NFS5, NFS6): a table of sound patches, then their wave data. Car banks (NFS2 `<car>.BNK` / `O<car>.BNK` (opponent) / `S<car>.BNK`, NFS3 `car.bnk` / `ocar.bnk` / `scar.bnk` in car.viv, NFS4 `careng.bnk` / `ocareng.bnk` / `scareng.bnk`, NFS3/NFS4 `GENCAR.BNK`, traffic `TRUCK.BNK`...) use indices 0 and 1 for the engine (looped), 2 for a one-shot with random detune range 200-250 (gear shift, like `gear` of TNFS car banks) and 3 for the horn (looped). Opponent banks have the engine and the horn only: NFS2 `O<car>.BNK` in slots 0 and 1 of a 2-slot table, NFS3 `ocar.bnk` / NFS4 `ocareng.bnk` in slots 0 and 3. NFS4 `careng.bnk` has more engine samples at higher indices (presumably one per RPM range). `W*.BNK` of NFS2 SE are car speech ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 4 | UTF-8 string. Always == "BNKl" | Resource ID |
| 4 | **version** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | 2 (NFS2, NFS2 SE, most of NFS3 GameData/Audio/SFX), 4 (NFS3 car.viv, NFS4, NFS5, NFS6) or 5 (NFS6) |
| 6 | **num_items** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Amount of slots in `items_descr` |
| 8 | **header_length** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Version 2 and 4: offset of the wave data, i.e. the length of the table and the patches. Version 5: file length |
| 12 | **wave_data_length** | 0..4 | Optional (if version >= 4): 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Version 4: length of the wave data. Version 5: 0 |
| 12..16 | **unk0** | 0..4 | Optional (if version >= 4): 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Unknown purpose |
| 12..20 | **items_descr** | num_items\*4 | Array of `num_items` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Offset of every patch, relative to its own position in this table, the array index being the sample index used by the game. 0 is an empty slot |
| 12 + num_items\*4..20 + num_items\*4 | **data_bytes** | up to end of block | Bytes | Sound patches ([EaSoundPatch](#easoundpatch)) at the offsets of `items_descr`, then wave data |
## **Geometries** ##
### **EaglModel** ###
#### **Size**: 52..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: EAGL model, used by NFS6 for track compartments, sky, cars and other geometry. A 32-bit little-endian MIPS ELF relocatable object file with model data in ".data" section, where named symbols point to render methods, vertex/index buffers and texture references ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **magic** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian). Always == 0x464c457f | ELF magic "\x7fELF" |
| 4 | **file_class** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | 1: 32-bit |
| 5 | **data_encoding** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | 1: little-endian |
| 6 | **elf_version** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Always 1 |
| 7 | **os_abi** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Always 0 |
| 8 | **padding** | 8 | Bytes | Zeros |
| 16 | **object_type** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | 1: relocatable object file |
| 18 | **machine** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | 8: MIPS |
| 20 | **version** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Always 1 |
| 24 | **entry** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Entry point, always 0 |
| 28 | **program_headers_offset** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Always 0, no program headers |
| 32 | **section_headers_offset** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Offset of section headers table |
| 36 | **flags** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | MIPS flags |
| 40 | **header_size** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Size of this header, 52 |
| 42 | **program_header_size** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Always 0 |
| 44 | **program_headers_count** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Always 0 |
| 46 | **section_header_size** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Size of section header, 40 |
| 48 | **section_headers_count** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Amount of sections |
| 50 | **section_names_index** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Index of the section with section names |
| 52 | **sections_data** | section_headers_offset - 52 | Bytes | Sections: ".data" with the model, ".shstrtab" and ".strtab" string tables, ".symtab" symbol table (16-byte records: name offset, value, size, info, other, section index) and ".rel.data" relocations of ".data" (8-byte records: offset, symbol index << 8 | type) |
| 52 + section_headers_offset - 52 | **section_headers** | section_headers_count\*40 | Array of `section_headers_count` items<br/>Item type: [EaglSectionHeader](#eaglsectionheader) | Section headers table |
| 52 + section_headers_offset - 52 + section_headers_count\*40 | **trailing_bytes** | up to end of file | Bytes | Zeros after section headers, usually none. Car "skeleton.o" has 40 of them: a section header slot of absent relocations section |
### **EaglSectionHeader** ###
#### **Size**: 40 bytes ####
#### **Description**: ELF32 section header ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **name_offset** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Offset of section name in the section names table |
| 4 | **section_type** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | 1: program data (".data"), 2: symbol table, 3: string table, 9: relocations |
| 8 | **flags** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Section flags |
| 12 | **address** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Virtual address, always 0 |
| 16 | **offset** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Offset of section data in the file |
| 20 | **size** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Size of section data in bytes |
| 24 | **link** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Index of related section (string table of symbol table) |
| 28 | **info** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Extra info (for relocations: index of the section the relocations apply to) |
| 32 | **alignment** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Section alignment |
| 36 | **entry_size** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Size of table entry, if section is a table |
## **Maps** ##
### **Nfs6AiPaths** ###
#### **Size**: 20..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: NFS6 race route (levelNN/aipaths.dat): the road graph for AI cars and the flight paths of the police helicopter. Opening it shows the route in 3D: the compartments listed in drvpath.ini next to it ("compNN.o" files in the parent folder) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **version** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Always 1 |
| 4 | **road_paths** | 8..? | [Nfs6AiPathGraph](#nfs6aipathgraph) | Roads for AI cars |
| 12..? | **helicopter_paths** | 8..? | [Nfs6AiPathGraph](#nfs6aipathgraph) | Flight paths of police helicopter |
### **Nfs6AiPathGraph** ###
#### **Size**: 8..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: A graph of paths ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **num_nodes** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Length of nodes array |
| 4 | **nodes** | num_nodes\*12 | Array of `num_nodes` items<br/>Item size: 12 bytes<br/>Item type: Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: Float number (little-endian) | Graph nodes: start and end positions of every path |
| 4 + num_nodes\*12 | **num_paths** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Length of paths array |
| 8 + num_nodes\*12 | **paths** | num_paths\*36..? | Array of `num_paths` items<br/>Item type: [Nfs6AiPath](#nfs6aipath) | Paths |
### **Nfs6AiPath** ###
#### **Size**: 36..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: A road between two graph nodes. Paths with the same start/end node positions are connected ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **name** | 16 | UTF-8 string | Path name, e.g. "AI_center011" |
| 16 | **start_node** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Index of the graph node where the path starts |
| 20 | **end_node** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Index of the graph node where the path ends |
| 24 | **unk0** | 4 | Float number (little-endian) | Always 44.703 |
| 28 | **path_type** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Shortcut difficulty: main road is 1, alternative roads and shortcuts 2..11. At a node, an AI racer takes the path of the highest difficulty up to its limit (NFSHP2.exe 0x4c4fc0, limit from Racer.MinPathDifficulty / Racer.MaxPathDifficulty of AI/racetune.ini and the racer), never one above 10 |
| 32 | **num_points** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Length of points array |
| 36 | **points** | num_points\*28 | Array of `num_points` items<br/>Item type: [Nfs6AiPathPoint](#nfs6aipathpoint) | Path points, from start node to end node |
### **Nfs6AiPathPoint** ###
#### **Size**: 28 bytes ####
#### **Description**: A point of the AI path ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **position** | 12 | Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: Float number (little-endian) | Point position, Y is up |
| 12 | **left_width** | 4 | Float number (little-endian) | Distance from the path to the left edge of the drivable area (usually 10) |
| 16 | **right_width** | 4 | Float number (little-endian) | Distance from the path to the right edge of the drivable area, negative (usually -10) |
| 20 | **unk0** | 4 | Float number (little-endian) | Values from -9 to 6, maybe road bank |
| 24 | **unk1** | 4 | Float number (little-endian) | Values from 35 to 60, maybe recommended speed |
## **Car specs** ##
### **Nfs6CarIni** ###
#### **Size**: ? bytes ####
#### **Description**: NFS Hot Pursuit 2 PC car physics, `car.ini`: the car as the player drives it (CarIni_Load 0x422bd0 with role 0 or 4: the player, network cars, traffic: the only file traffic cars have). HCVehicle_Load 0x415030 copies the values of a car of the same type already loaded (0x4de9f0), else CarIni_Load 0x422bd0 picks the file by the car's role: car_hp.ini for role 1 or while 0x83a5f4 is set (hot pursuit), car_cop.ini for role 3 or while 0x83a5f8 is set, carracer.ini for role 2 (AI racers), car.ini otherwise; the four files have the same keys. Sections read in order: [basic] (0x420020), [engineblock] (0x4218b0), [transmission] (0x421120), [rearend], [brake_front] / [brake_rear] (0x422060), [tire_front] / [tire_rear] (0x4222c0), [horn]; [audio] by the sound setup (0x51b990). INI rules: `resources/eac/ini.py` `parse_ini` (EA CINI parser 0x5b5180: no comment syntax, keys ignoring case, the first of repeated sections) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **basic** | ? | [Nfs6CarIniBasic](#nfs6carinibasic) | Body, aerodynamics, steering, drive layout and suspension |
| ? | **display_data** | ? | [Nfs6CarIniDisplayData](#nfs6carinidisplaydata) | Front end text ids of the car's figures; not read (the front end takes them from Cars.ini) |
| ? | **engineblock** | ? | [Nfs6CarIniEngineblock](#nfs6cariniengineblock) | Engine: rpm range, torque curve, sound |
| ? | **transmission** | ? | [Nfs6CarIniTransmission](#nfs6carinitransmission) | Gearbox |
| ? | **rearend** | ? | [Nfs6CarIniRearend](#nfs6carinirearend) | Final drive |
| ? | **tire_rear** | ? | [Nfs6CarIniTireRear](#nfs6carinitirerear) | Rear tyres (record by `attach`) |
| ? | **tire_front** | ? | [Nfs6CarIniTireFront](#nfs6carinitirefront) | Front tyres (record by `attach`) |
| ? | **brake_rear** | ? | [Nfs6CarIniBrakeRear](#nfs6carinibrakerear) | Rear brakes (record by `attach`) |
| ? | **brake_front** | ? | [Nfs6CarIniBrakeFront](#nfs6carinibrakefront) | Front brakes (record by `attach`) |
| ? | **horn** | ? | [Nfs6CarIniHorn](#nfs6carinihorn) | Horn sound (not in the shipped files) |
| ? | **skins** | ? | [Nfs6CarIniSkins](#nfs6cariniskins) | Not read |
| ? | **audio** | ? | [Nfs6CarIniAudio](#nfs6cariniaudio) | Sounds (read by the sound setup, not the physics) |
| ? | **render** | ? | [Nfs6CarIniRender](#nfs6carinirender) | Not read |
| ? | **addon** | ? | [Nfs6CarIniAddon](#nfs6cariniaddon) | Not read |
| ? | **other_sections** | ? | Array of `None` items<br/>Item type: [IniOtherSection](#iniothersection) | Sections the definition does not name, and repeated sections after the first (lookups find the first), in file order. The game reads none of them |

### **Nfs6CarRacerIni** ###
#### **Size**: ? bytes ####
#### **Description**: NFS Hot Pursuit 2 PC car physics, `carracer.ini`: the car as an AI racer (role 2). HCVehicle_Load 0x415030 copies the values of a car of the same type already loaded (0x4de9f0), else CarIni_Load 0x422bd0 picks the file by the car's role: car_hp.ini for role 1 or while 0x83a5f4 is set (hot pursuit), car_cop.ini for role 3 or while 0x83a5f8 is set, carracer.ini for role 2 (AI racers), car.ini otherwise; the four files have the same keys. INI rules: `resources/eac/ini.py` `parse_ini` (EA CINI parser 0x5b5180: no comment syntax, keys ignoring case, the first of repeated sections) ####

### **Nfs6EngineAudioTable** ###
#### **Size**: 360..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: NFS Hot Pursuit 2 PC engine sound table ("CRDl"), an item of `Cars/cartable.viv`. EngineAudio_Load 0x4355e0 loads `engine.ltb`, `engine.ctb` and `engine.rpm` (`engine.htb` / `engine.btb` are never loaded) and EngineAudio_RelocateTables 0x4354c0 turns the table offsets into pointers (flag +5). EngineAudio_Update 0x4349e0 plays up to 16 engine samples at once: the 8 slots of engine.ctb (the engine without load) and the 8 of engine.ltb (under load), crossfaded by the engine load; each slot's volume table is read at the sound index = (rpm - MinRPM) x 127 / (RedLine - MinRPM) (0x435430, 0..127) and its pitch table bends the sample (64 = its own pitch). engine.rpm (one slot, identity table) is loaded but only checked for presence: the FakeRPM debug line shows the same index ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **magic** | 4 | UTF-8 string. Always == "CRDl" | Magic "CRDl" |
| 4 | **version** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | 2 in every file |
| 5 | **relocated** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Set to 1 by the game once the offsets are pointers (0x4354c0); 0 in the files |
| 6 | **unk0** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | 0 in every file |
| 7 | **unk1** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | 0 (engine.rpm) or 100 |
| 8 | **header_values** | 24 | Array of `12` items<br/>Item size: 2 bytes<br/>Item type: 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Header values, the same in every file (20, 15, 500, 0, 200, 0, 100, 40, 300, 0, 100, 0: 16-bit words); no reader found |
| 32 | **slots** | 8 | Array of `8` items<br/>Item size: 1 byte<br/>Item type: 1-byte signed integer | Engine sample of each slot: index of the patch in the car's engine sound bank (cxhi, cxmd, cxid, cehi... / lxhi...), -1 = slot unused; the game counts slots up to the last used one |
| 40 | **reserved** | 256 | Array of `256` items<br/>Item size: 1 byte<br/>Item type: 1-byte unsigned integer | Zeros in every file |
| 296 | **volume_table_offsets** | 32 | Array of `8` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Per slot: offset of its volume table from this entry (pointer = entry address + value), 0 for an unused slot |
| 328 | **pitch_table_offsets** | 32 | Array of `8` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Per slot: offset of its pitch table from this entry, 0 for an unused slot |
| 360 | **tables** | ((file size - 0x168) / 512)\*512 | Array of `(file size - 0x168) / 512` items<br/>Item size: 512 bytes<br/>Item type: Array of `512` items<br/>Item size: 1 byte<br/>Item type: 1-byte signed integer | The tables, 512 signed bytes each: volume 0..127 per sound index, pitch (64 = the sample's pitch) per sound index; the game reads entries 0..127 |
| 360 + ((file size - 0x168) / 512)\*512 | **trailing** | rest | Array of `rest` items<br/>Item size: 1 byte<br/>Item type: 1-byte unsigned integer | Bytes after the last whole table (none in the files) |
### **Nfs6CarIniBasic** ###
#### **Size**: ? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Body, aerodynamics, steering, drive layout and suspension ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **Mass** | ? | Float (`%f`), kg | Car mass, kg. CarIni_ReadBasic 0x420020 -> HCVehicle +0x208; +0x20c (unsprung mass) = Mass x 0.1. Each brake section adds 8 kg and each tyre section 12 kg to both (0x422bd0, 0x4222c0), so the simulated mass is Mass + 40 kg. Used for the wheel loads (Mass / 4 per wheel, HCVehicle_SetupWheels 0x414a50; axle loads 0x419a40), the roll terms of the sprung mass (Mass - unsprung, 0x415a30, 0x4271a0) and the automatic gearbox (0x415780). Required. |
| ? | **PercentUnsprungMass** | ? | Float (`%f`) | Not read by NFSHP2.exe (no such string in the executable). |
| ? | **BodyShape** | ? | Integer (`%d`) | Mass distribution of the body for its inertia. CarIni_ReadBasic 0x420020 -> +0x228; HCVehicle_SetupInertia 0x415570 picks the pitch and roll factors of the inertia tensor (pitch = (height^2 + length^2) x mass x factor, roll = (width^2 + height^2) x mass x factor / 3, from the body box): 1, 3, 7: pitch 0.60, roll 0.70; 4, 5: 0.65, 0.85; 6: 0.65, 0.80; any other: 0.83, 0.84. Shipped: 0, 1, 3, 4, 6. Required. |
| ? | **WheelBase** | ? | Float (`%f`), m | Distance between the axles, m. CarIni_ReadBasic 0x420020 -> +0x210: axles at +/- WheelBase / 2 (HCVehicle_SetupGeometry 0x415a30), the steering lock atan(WheelBase / TurningCircleRadius), the pitch limits atan(Travel / WheelBase), the aerodynamic pitch moment (0x424660). Required. |
| ? | **FrontTrackWidth** | ? | Float (`%f`), m | Front track, m. CarIni_ReadBasic 0x420020 -> +0x214: front wheels at x = -/+ FrontTrackWidth / 2 (0x414a50); frontal area = VehicleHeight x FrontTrackWidth x 0.8 (0x415a30). Required. |
| ? | **RearTrackWidth** | ? | Float (`%f`), m | Rear track, m. CarIni_ReadBasic 0x420020 -> +0x218: rear wheels at x = +/- RearTrackWidth / 2 (0x414a50). Required. |
| ? | **VehicleHeight** | ? | Float (`%f`), m | Body height, m. CarIni_ReadBasic 0x420020 -> +0x21c: frontal area for the air drag = VehicleHeight x FrontTrackWidth x 0.8 (0x415a30). Required. |
| ? | **HeightOfGravity** | ? | Float (`%f`), m | Height of the centre of gravity, m. CarIni_ReadBasic 0x420020 -> +0x220: the rigid body's centre of gravity height (0x415a30), load transfer of the drag (x 0.909, 0x424660) and the roll terms (0.455 / 0.318 / 0.591 x height x g x sprung mass against the roll stiffnesses, 0x415a30). Required. |
| ? | **RearSlideFactor** | ? | Float (`%f`) | Rear slide damping (driving aid). CarIni_ReadBasic 0x420020 -> +0x234 = max(value, 0); missing: 0.85. HCVehicle_Update 0x424f70: while it is above 0, the car is on the ground and faster than 6 m/s, each step takes value / 30 of the rear's sideways speed away when it slides against the steering. 0 in car.ini / car_hp.ini, 1.85..6.2 in carracer.ini (AI racers) and car_cop.ini. |
| ? | **FrontGripBias** | ? | Float (`%f`) | Front axle's share of the static weight, 0..1. CarIni_ReadBasic 0x420020 -> +0x224: the centre of gravity is (1 - value) x WheelBase behind the front axle (+0x70) and value x WheelBase ahead of the rear one (+0x74, 0x415a30); static axle loads (0x419830, 0x419a40). Required. |
| ? | **AISpeedFactor** | ? | Float (`%f`) | CarIni_ReadBasic 0x420020 -> +0x240, clamped to 0..1; missing: 1.0 (error logged, not required). No reader of the value found: no float load of HCVehicle +0x240 in the executable. |
| ? | **AeroDragCoefficient** | ? | Float (`%f`) | Air drag coefficient (Cd). CarIni_ReadBasic 0x420020 -> +0x1f4: drag force = 0.601 x Cd x frontal area x speed^2 (HCVehicle_AeroDrag 0x424660, 0.601 = air density / 2), also in the automatic gearbox's shift speeds (0x415780). Each tyre section wider than 215 mm adds min((width - 215) x 0.00004, 0.005) (0x4222c0). Required. |
| ? | **AeroFrontDownforceCoefficient** | ? | Float (`%f`), kg per m/s | Front downforce, kg-force per m/s of speed on the front axle. CarIni_ReadBasic 0x420020 -> +0x1f8: each front wheel gets value x |speed| x 9.81 x 0.5 N (HCVehicle_Downforce 0x424530): linear in speed. Required. |
| ? | **AeroRearDownforceCoefficient** | ? | Float (`%f`), kg per m/s | Rear downforce, kg-force per m/s on the rear axle. CarIni_ReadBasic 0x420020 -> +0x1fc: each rear wheel gets value x |speed| x 9.81 x 0.5 N (0x424530). Required. |
| ? | **BodyLiftCoefficient** | ? | Float (`%f`) | Lift coefficient. CarIni_ReadBasic 0x420020 -> +0x200: with the four wheels on the ground each wheel load changes by -0.601 x value x frontal area x speed^2 / 4 (0x424660): positive values lift the car (less grip), negative ones press it. Required. |
| ? | **UnderBodyDragCoefficient** | ? | Float (`%f`) | CarIni_ReadBasic 0x420020 -> +0x204; missing: 1.1. HCVehicle_UnderbodyDrag 0x424430: while the body touches the ground and the car moves down, an upward force 0.601 x value x vertical speed^2 x the body's floor area x 4 slows the fall. |
| ? | **SpeedGovernor** | ? | Float (`%f`), m/s | Top speed limit, m/s, 0 = none. CarIni_ReadBasic 0x420020 -> +0x23c; missing: 0. Engine_Update 0x429210: at or above it the engine gives no drive torque and its rpm is held at the gear's rpm of that speed. Shipped: 0 in car.ini, the racers' top speeds in carracer.ini (55.88..107.29). |
| ? | **TurningCircleRadius** | ? | Float (`%f`), m | Turning radius, m. CarIni_ReadBasic 0x420020 -> +0x24c: full steering lock = atan(WheelBase / radius) (+0x7c, 0x415a30). Required. |
| ? | **TurninRamp** | ? | Float (`%f`) | Steering speed. CarIni_ReadBasic 0x420020 -> +0x250 = value / 128. HCVehicle_Steering 0x4286f0: per physics step the wheel position (-1..1) moves towards the input by at most value / 128, while input and wheel are on the same side of the centre. Required. |
| ? | **TurnoutRamp** | ? | Float (`%f`) | Steering speed back across the centre. CarIni_ReadBasic 0x420020 -> +0x254 = value / 128 (0x4286f0): the step limit while the input is on the other side of the centre than the wheel. Required. |
| ? | **BaseDampingVelocity** | ? | Float (`%f`), m/s | Speed where the steering limit starts, m/s. CarIni_ReadBasic 0x420020 -> +0x258; missing: 8.9406 (20 mph). HCVehicle_SteeringLimit 0x4289a0: f = clamp((|speed| - base) / range, 0, 1); the wheel position is f x input^2 + (1 - f) x |input| and at most DampingLimit x f + 1 - f of full lock (counter-steering into a slide may go further). |
| ? | **RangeDampingVelocity** | ? | Float (`%f`), m/s | Speed range over which the steering limit comes in, m/s. CarIni_ReadBasic 0x420020 -> +0x25c; missing: 22.3515 (50 mph) (0x4289a0). |
| ? | **DampingLimit** | ? | Float (`%f`) | Steering range left above BaseDampingVelocity + RangeDampingVelocity, fraction of full lock. CarIni_ReadBasic 0x420020 -> +0x260; missing: 1.0 (0x4289a0). |
| ? | **DampeningLimit** | ? | Float (`%f`) | Not read by NFSHP2.exe (a misspelling of DampingLimit). |

| ? | **PowerSteering** | ? | Integer (`%d`) | Not read by NFSHP2.exe (no such string in the executable). |

HCVehicle_SetupWheels 0x414a50 keeps it only for four driven wheels; front wheels only: 1, otherwise 0. Each front wheel gets value / 2, each rear one (1 - value) / 2 (HCVehicle_SetupDrivetrain 0x415d30). Required. |
| ? | **driveWheels** | ? | 4 keys `driveWheels_%d` (from 0), one value each<br/>Item size: ? bytes<br/>Item type: Integer (`%d`) | Driven wheels, 0 / 1: 0 front left, 1 front right, 2 rear right, 3 rear left. CarIni_ReadBasic 0x420020 -> bytes +0x238..; all 0: the rear ones. Each key required. |
| ? | **YawInertiaFactor** | ? | Float (`%f`) | Scale of the yaw inertia. CarIni_ReadBasic 0x420020 -> +0x264, clamped to 0.3..2; missing: 1.0. 0x415570: yaw inertia = (length^2 + width^2) x mass x 0.8 x value. |

### **Nfs6CarIniEngineblock** ###
#### **Size**: ? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Engine: rpm range, torque curve, sound ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **FlyWheelInertiaFactor** | ? | Float (`%f`) | Scale of the engine's inertia. CarIni_ReadEngine 0x4218b0 -> +0x300; missing: 1.0 (error logged). Engine inertia = 0.18077 x value kg m^2 (HCVehicle_SetupDrivetrain 0x415d30). |
| ? | **mass** | ? | Float (`%f`) | Not read by NFSHP2.exe (the exe reads `Mass` in [basic] only). |
| ? | **MinRPM** | ? | Integer (`%d`), rpm | Idle rpm. CarIni_ReadEngine 0x4218b0 -> +0x290: the engine never turns slower (0x414f20, Engine_Update 0x429210), the drive is zero below it (0x419700), engine sounds play from it (0x435430: sound index = (rpm - MinRPM) x 127 / (RedLine - MinRPM)). Required. |
| ? | **RedLine** | ? | Integer (`%d`), rpm | Maximum rpm. CarIni_ReadEngine 0x4218b0 -> +0x294: each gear's rpm per m/s comes from its speed at the red line (Gearbox_ComputeRpmPerMps 0x419550), no drive above it (0x419700), top of the engine sound tables. Required. |
| ? | **WarningLine** | ? | Integer (`%d`), rpm | CarIni_ReadEngine 0x4218b0 -> +0x304 = min(value, RedLine); missing: RedLine x 7 / 8 (error logged). No reader of the value found. |
| ? | **torqueCurve** | ? | 25 keys `torqueCurve_%d` (from 0), one value each<br/>Item size: ? bytes<br/>Item type: Float (`%f`), N m | Full throttle torque, N m, entry i at i x 500 rpm, linear in between (Engine_TorqueAtRpm 0x41fde0). CarIni_ReadEngine 0x4218b0 reads 25 entries (0..24) -> +0x29c; a missing one logs an error and is 0 (every shipped file stops at 23). Past the last non-zero entry the reader fills the curve falling: each entry the last one times r, r squared every step, r = the last decrease ratio of the curve (0.8 when it never decreased). |
| ? | **dbAudio** | ? | 6 keys `dbAudio_%d` (from 0), one value each<br/>Item size: ? bytes<br/>Item type: Text (up to 3 characters kept) | Engine sound codes. CarIni_ReadEngine 0x4218b0 reads only dbAudio_1 (required; 3 characters kept, `NULL` = none) into +0x298 (0x41fd90), the engine sound bank code. dbAudio_0, _2.._5 are not read. |
| ? | **attach** | ? | Integer (`%d`) | Not read by NFSHP2.exe (the exe reads `attach` in the brake and tyre sections only). |
| ? | **basename** | ? | Text | Not read by NFSHP2.exe (no such string in the executable). |
| ? | **displayname** | ? | Text | Not read by NFSHP2.exe (the exe reads `displayname` in Cars.ini only). |

| 0 | **Mass** | ? | Float (`%f`) | Not read by NFSHP2.exe (the exe reads `Mass` in [basic] only). |
| ? | **NumberOfGears** | ? | Integer (`%d`) | Gears with reverse and neutral (8 = R, N, 6 forward). CarIni_ReadTransmission 0x421120 -> +0x30c. Required. |
| ? | **GearShiftDelay** | ? | Integer (`%d`), steps | Shift time in physics steps. CarIni_ReadTransmission 0x421120 -> +0x310 = value, + 12 with the manual gearbox; the clutch engages over it (0x4290c0, 0x42a010). Required. |
| ? | **Automatic** | ? | Integer (`%d`) | Not read by NFSHP2.exe (the gearbox is the player's choice, passed to CarIni_Load 0x422bd0). |
| ? | **GearRatios** | ? | 8 keys `GearRatios_%d` (from 0), one value each<br/>Item size: ? bytes<br/>Item type: Float (`%f`) | Gear ratios: 0 reverse, 1 neutral (0), 2.. forward. CarIni_ReadTransmission 0x421120 -> +0x314; a missing one logs an error and is 0. Rpm per m/s = ratio x max(FinalGearRatio, FrontFinalGearRatio) x 60 / rear tyre circumference (0x419550; reverse negative); drive force = torque x ratio x final x efficiency / rear tyre radius (0x419700). |
| ? | **GearEfficiency** | ? | 8 keys `GearEfficiency_%d` (from 0), one value each<br/>Item size: ? bytes<br/>Item type: Float (`%f`) | Efficiency of each gear, 0..1. CarIni_ReadTransmission 0x421120 -> +0x334 (x 0.97 with the automatic gearbox); missing: 1 (error logged); clamped to 0..1 by 0x415a30. Scales the drive force. |
| ? | **TorqueConverterRatio** | ? | Float (`%f`) | CarIni_ReadTransmission 0x421120 -> +0x384; missing: 0 (error logged). No reader: no load of +0x384 in the executable. |
| ? | **TorqueConverterMaxRPM** | ? | Integer (`%d`) | CarIni_ReadTransmission 0x421120 -> +0x388; missing: 0 (error logged). No reader: no load of +0x388 in the executable. |
| ? | **GearShiftPointCoefficient** | ? | Float (`%f`) | Automatic up-shift point. CarIni_ReadTransmission 0x421120 -> +0x38c, clamped to 0.75..1.2; missing: 0.9 (error logged). Gearbox_ShiftSpeed 0x415780: up-shift speed = value x the speed from which the next gear accelerates more (drive minus air drag and rolling resistance); when they never cross, 70 % (1st) or 75 % of the red line. |

## **Images** ##
### **EacImage** ###
#### **Size**: 16..? bytes ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 1 | Enum of 256 possible values<br/><details><summary>Value names:</summary>64 (0x40): 4Bit PS1<br/>96 (0x60): DXT1 compressed bitmap<br/>97 (0x61): DXT3 compressed bitmap<br/>98 (0x62): DXT5 compressed bitmap<br/>109 (0x6d): 16Bit_4444 color format bitmap<br/>120 (0x78): 16Bit_0565 color format bitmap<br/>121 (0x79): 4Bit (swapped)<br/>122 (0x7a): 4Bit<br/>123 (0x7b): 8Bit<br/>125 (0x7d): 32Bit color format bitmap<br/>126 (0x7e): 16Bit_1555 color format bitmap<br/>127 (0x7f): 24Bit color format bitmap</details> | Resource ID |
| 1 | **next_offset** | 3 | 3-bytes signed integer (little endian) | Offset from the start of the image to the first block attached to it: the palette of an 8Bit image, hot spots (0x7C), text (0x6F), and in NFS6 0x69 / 0x70 blocks. Every attached block starts with its id and the offset to the next one (0 in the last), so they make a chain, which this parser follows. 0 when nothing is attached (then an 8Bit image uses !pal or !PAL of the SHPI), never the size of the image block. Recomputed on save when a block parsed into a field is attached. TNFS has other values in a few car (CFM) and track (FAM) textures without attached blocks: mostly a negative offset to the !PAL item of the SHPI, sometimes garbage |
| 4 | **width** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Bitmap width in pixels |
| 6 | **height** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Bitmap height in pixels |
| 8 | **pivot** | 4 | Point in 2D space (x,y), where each coordinate is: 2-bytes signed integer (little endian) | TNFS dashboards add both coordinates to the points of `hot_spots`. y coordinate is used by the horizon bitmap "horz" of TNFS FAM files when the game scrolls it (horizon "ring type" 0, the open road tracks by default): this row of the bitmap lies on the horizon line (Win95 SE FUN_0043ae64). The horizon ring (ring type 1, the closed tracks) does not use it |
| 12 | **position** | 4 | Point in 2D space (x,y), where each coordinate is: 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Bitmap position on screen. Used for menu/dash sprites. In NFS5 FSH files this is the position of the image in a texture page (atlas), which is used by CRP models: 12 lower bits of each coordinate are a signed value, 4 higher bits of y are the amount of `mipmaps` levels (always all of them down to 1x1, 0 without mipmaps), set on save |
| 16 | **bitmap** | width \* height \* pixel_byteness | Bytes | Pixel color table. For 8Bit bitmap each value represents an index of color in the attached palette. Palette can be stored: <br/>- right after 8Bit image<br/>- as !pal/!PAL in the same SHPI<br/>- in a different SHPI before this one (if it is WWWW archive)<br/>- even in different QFS file (TNFS, CONTROL directory).<br/>Color model is selected according to `resource_id` field. Color models are described [here](eac_colors.md). DXT1/DXT3/DXT5 bitmaps are S3TC-compressed 4x4 pixel blocks (8, 16 and 16 bytes per block) |
| 16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness | **mipmaps** | 0..(1/4 + 1/16 + 1/64 + etc) \* width \* height \* pixel_byteness | Optional (if dimensions are powers of two and position.y has the amount of levels): Bytes | Mipmaps pixel data in the same format as `bitmap` field. There are images with sizes w/2 x h/2, w/4 x h/4, .... up to 1x1, in descending order, each padded with zeros to 16 bytes. Only NFS5 files have them: the 4 high bits of `position.y` hold the amount of levels |
| 16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness..16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness + (1/4 + 1/16 + 1/64 + etc) \* width \* height \* pixel_byteness | **pad** | 0..up to offset next_offset | Optional (if next_offset points past the pixels): Padding bytes | Bytes between the pixels (and mipmaps) and the first attached block: zeros, or leftovers aligning it |
| 16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness..16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness + (1/4 + 1/16 + 1/64 + etc) \* width \* height \* pixel_byteness + up to offset next_offset | **embedded_palette** | 0..? | Optional (if the chain of attached blocks has a palette here): [EacPalette](#eacpalette) | Embedded palette, which should be assigned to this bitmap (except for ga00 in TR2_001.FAM) |
| 16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness..? | **embedded_palette_pad** | 0..up to the next attached block | Optional (if the next attached block is 0x7C or 0x6F, not right here): Bytes | Bytes between the embedded palette and the next attached block |
| 16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness..? | **hot_spots** | 0..? | Optional (if the chain of attached blocks has 0x7C here): [ShpiHotSpots](#shpihotspots) | Hot spots: points of interest of the bitmap, read by TNFS dashboards |
| 16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness..? | **hot_spots_pad** | 0..up to the next attached block | Optional (if the next attached block is 0x7C or 0x6F, not right here): Bytes | Bytes between the hot spots and the next attached block |
| 16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness..? | **text** | 0..? | Optional (if the chain of attached blocks has 0x6F here): [ShpiText](#shpitext) | Shpi text |
| 16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness..? | **embedded_palette_2** | 0..? | Optional (if palette header after the end of the chain): [EacPalette](#eacpalette) | A palette after the last attached block, which no block links to (some textures of TNFS TR* tracks) |
| 16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness..? | **embedded_palette_3** | 0..? | Optional (if palette header after the end of the chain): [EacPalette](#eacpalette) | One more palette which no block links to |
| 16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness..? | **embedded_palette_4** | 0..? | Optional (if palette header after the end of the chain): [EacPalette](#eacpalette) | One more palette which no block links to |
### **EacPalette** ###
#### **Size**: 16..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Resource with colors LUT (look-up table). EA 8-bit bitmaps have 1-byte value per pixel, meaning the index of color in LUT of assigned palette. Has special colors: 255th in most cases means transparent color, 254th in TNFS car textures is replaced by tail light color, 250th - 253th are the cop car light bar (TNFS maps them to the VGA palette entries 0xFA - 0xFD: red, dark red, blue, dark blue, swapped every 16 clock ticks during a police chase, Win95 SE `gfx_draw_car_model` 0x458d4c) and are rendered black in other cars. The converter writes these colors to `car_colors.json` next to the PNGs.<br/>TNFS car models (CFM) have a second palette `!xxx` next to `!PAL` in the high-poly textures SHPI (TRAFFC in both): the car's slice of the shared 256-color VGA palette in 8-bit modes (Win95 SE `gfx_car_palettes_setup` 0x4572e0). Its first 23 colors (8 for traffic, 24 for the player in a single race / tournament) go to the car's palette entries (player 0x30, opponent 0x48, traffic 0x60 + 8 * slot), then the textures are remapped from `!PAL` to the nearest colors of the VGA palette. `!PAL` is the palette of the textures, `!xxx` is never used to draw them. Cops get none, and the `M*.CFM` models (opponents of a single race / tournament, which share `CARFAMS/CARPAL.FSH` instead) have junk there. Many `!xxx` have the 8-bit bitmap id 0x7B (256x1 or 256x3) instead of a palette id. The converter writes its used colors to `car_colors.json` (`palette_slice`) instead of a file of its own ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 1 | Enum of 256 possible values<br/><details><summary>Value names:</summary>34 (0x22): 24BitDos color format palette<br/>36 (0x24): 24Bit color format palette<br/>41 (0x29): 16Bit_0565 color format palette<br/>42 (0x2a): 32Bit color format palette<br/>45 (0x2d): 16Bit_1555 color format palette</details> | Resource ID |
| 1 | **next_offset** | 3 | 3-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | When attached to a bitmap: offset from the start of this block to the next block attached to the same bitmap (0 when this is the last one). Recomputed on save when a block parsed into a field follows. 0 in palette items (`!pal`) |
| 4 | **num_colors** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Amount of colors |
| 6 | **unk1** | 2 | Bytes | Unknown purpose |
| 8 | **num_colors1** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Equals to num_colors, except for some CRP structures in NFS5 |
| 10 | **unk2** | 6 | Bytes | Unknown purpose |
| 16 | **colors** | ? | Type according to enum `resource_id`:<br/>- Array of `num_colors` items<br/>Item size: 3 bytes<br/>Item type: 3-bytes unsigned integer (big endian)<br/>- Array of `num_colors` items<br/>Item size: 3 bytes<br/>Item type: 3-bytes unsigned integer (big endian)<br/>- Array of `num_colors` items<br/>Item size: 2 bytes<br/>Item type: 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian)<br/>- Array of `num_colors` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian)<br/>- Array of `num_colors` items<br/>Item size: 2 bytes<br/>Item type: 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Colors LUT. Color model is selected according to `resource_id` field. Color models are described [here](eac_colors.md) |
### **ShpiHotSpots** ###
#### **Size**: 8..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: A list of hot spots: points of interest of the bitmap it is attached to (after the bitmap and its embedded palette), the index of a point gives its meaning. Many bitmaps of menus, track (FAM) and car (CFM) textures have an empty list, others in the same files have none, and 1x1 placeholder bitmaps of dashboards have copies of the list of another bitmap. TNFS reads it in the dashboard loader only (DOS `tnfs_dash_000522be`, Win95 SE FUN_0041f9a0, the demo `tnfs_dashboard_load`; PSX and 3DO do not read FSH dashboards), from four bitmaps of `SIMDATA/DASH/*DH.FSH` / `*DL.FSH`:<br/>- `dash`: 10 points. 0, 1 = top left and bottom right corners of the rear-view mirror; 2 = radar detector power light; 3..7 = the 5 radar detector level lights; 8, 9 = the loader turns them into offsets from 2 and 3, nothing reads them<br/>- `tach`: tachometer needle tip at 0, 1024, 2048... RPM, the last point is the needle centre. The needle (Win95 SE FUN_00420d0c) is a line from the centre to a tip interpolated linearly between consecutive points: index = RPM >> 10, fraction = (RPM & 1023) / 1024. Nothing clamps the index to the list<br/>- `sped`: speedometer needle tip at 0, 10, 20... mph (0, 20, 40... km/h in the German version), the last point is the needle centre. Drawn as `tach`, from the speed rounded to whole mph (km/h): index = speed / 10 (/ 20), fraction = remainder / 10 (/ 20), the index not clamped either. The loader overwrites point 12 with the midpoint of points 11 and 13 (integer division) for every car: in `SIMDATA/DASH` and `SIMDATA/GDASH` `TSUPRADH.FSH`, `DVIPERDH.FSH` and `CZR1DH.FSH` point 12 holds garbage (x values like 1684369933). The cars with a digital speedometer draw digits instead<br/>- `gate`: gear lever knob position for every gear: 0 = reverse, 1 = neutral, then gears from 1st: 7 or 8 points. The game reads 9 points (a 9th, where present, is at the corner of the bitmap)<br/>The game walks the attached blocks until it finds 0x7C, so it hangs when one of these bitmaps has no hot spots ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer. Always == 0x7c | Resource ID |
| 1 | **next_offset** | 3 | 3-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Offset from the start of this block to the next block attached to the same bitmap (0 when this is the last one). Recomputed on save when a block parsed into a field follows |
| 4 | **num_points** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Length of points array |
| 8 | **points** | num_points\*8 | Array of `num_points` items<br/>Item size: 8 bytes<br/>Item type: Point in 2D space (x,y), where each coordinate is: 4-bytes signed integer (little endian) | Points in screen pixels, relative to the bitmap: the screen point is `position` + `pivot` + point, so `pivot` + point is the pixel of the bitmap. TNFS reads the low byte of the amount only |
### **ShpiText** ###
#### **Size**: 8..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Text attached to an SHPI image. In the NFS3 / NFS4 sky archives (`SKY.FSH`, `sky.qfs`) the `SUN*` images carry the sun sprite settings: the numbers after `A` (azimuth, degrees), `B` and `R` (the sprite's corners are 10 * R from its centre) and the words `ROTATE`, `NOADD` (not additive), `INFRONT` (drawn after the clouds) (nfs3.exe 0x47a970, nfs4.exe 0x4c9050, which reads it only when `Tr.ini` has no `hasSun=1`). Elsewhere the purpose is unclear ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer. Always == 0x6f | Resource ID |
| 1 | **next_offset** | 3 | 3-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Offset from the start of this block to the next block attached to the same bitmap (0 when this is the last one). Recomputed on save when a block parsed into a field follows |
| 4 | **len_text** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Length of 'text' utf8 block |
| 8 | **text** | len_text | UTF-8 string | Text contents |
## **Fonts** ##
### **FfnFont** ###
#### **Size**: 48..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Bitmap font: a font atlas bitmap plus glyph definitions (position and size of each symbol in the atlas) and optional kerning table ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 4 | UTF-8 string. One of ['"FNTF"', '"FNTP"', '"FNTS"', '"FNTX"', '"FNTM"', '"FNTG"', '"FNTA"', '"FntF"', '"FntP"', '"FntS"', '"FntX"', '"FntM"', '"FntG"', '"FntA"'] | Resource ID |
| 4 | **block_size** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | The length of this FFN block in bytes. Does not include the embedded palette of an 8Bit bitmap (and padding to it after bitmap data); the palette of a 4Bit bitmap (NFS6) is included. For older versions (I set version <= 101, but it can be anywhere up to < 309), "padding_2" length not included as well |
| 8 | **version** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Font format version. Defines the layout of glyph definitions (see [GlyphDefinition](#glyphdefinition)): 11 bytes below 200, 12 bytes up to 309 (last one padding), 12 bytes with `num_kern` above 309, 16 bytes from 321 with the `format` flag 16-bytes. Changing it changes the size of every glyph definition. Game fonts: 100 / 101 (TNFS to NFS4), 309 to 366 (NFS6) |
| 10 | **num_glyphs** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Amount of symbols, defined in this font |
| 12 | **flags** | 4 | Sub-byte compound block (little endian):<br/>13-bits int "pad"<br/>1-bits enum:<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 0: 12-bytes<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 1: 16-bytes<br/>2-bits enum:<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 0: ASCII<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 1: Unicode<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 2: Shift-JIS<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 3: Reserved<br/>4-bits int "layoutpad"<br/>1-bits enum:<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 0: LTR<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 1: RTL<br/>1-bits enum:<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 0: Horizontal<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 1: Vertical<br/>2-bits enum:<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 0: Roman (english)<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 1: Ideographic (Kanji)<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 2: Hanging (Arabic)<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 3: Unknown<br/>4-bits int "drawpad"<br/>1-bit flag "vram"<br/>1-bit flag "outline"<br/>1-bit flag "dropshadow"<br/>1-bit flag "antialiased" | Font flags: format of glyph definitions, encoding, layout and draw attributes |
| 16 | **center** | 2 | Point in 2D space (x,y), where each coordinate is: 1-byte unsigned integer | Unknown purpose |
| 18 | **ascent** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Distance from the baseline to the top of the glyphs in pixels. `ascent + descent` is the line height, and a glyph is drawn `y_offset` below the top of its line. NFS6 capitals end at `ascent`; TNFS and NFS2 fonts have `descent` 0 and keep the whole line height here |
| 19 | **descent** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Distance from the baseline to the bottom of the glyphs in pixels: NFS6 descenders end at `ascent + descent` |
| 20 | **definitions_ptr** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Pointer to definitions block |
| 24 | **kernings_ptr** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Pointer to kernings. 0 if there is no kernings table |
| 28 | **bdata_ptr** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Pointer to bitmap block |
| 32 | **padding_0** | up to offset definitions_ptr | Padding bytes | Unknown purpose |
| definitions_ptr | **definitions** | num_glyphs\*11..num_glyphs\*17 | Array of `num_glyphs` items<br/>Item type: [GlyphDefinition](#glyphdefinition) | Definitions of chars in this bitmap font, sorted by `code` (the writer keeps this order, stable sort by `code`) |
| ? | **padding_1** | 0..up to offset kernings_ptr | Optional (if kernings_ptr != 0): Padding bytes | Unknown purpose |
| ? | **kernings** | 0..? | Optional (if kernings_ptr != 0): Array, prefixed with length field<br/>Length field type: 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian)<br/>Item type: [KerningItem](#kerningitem) | Kerning pairs table. For versions > 309 (glyphs with `num_kern`) the pairs are sorted by right glyph, so the pairs of one right glyph follow each other: the writer keeps this order (stable sort by `right`) |
| ? | **padding_2** | up to offset bdata_ptr | Padding bytes | Puts the bitmap at the offset the game files use: versions < 309 at a multiple of 16 (gap filled with 0xAD; NFS2 SWISS36 at a multiple of 8), newer ones so that the pixels after the 16-byte bitmap header start at a multiple of 128 (gap starts with "Buy ERTS", then zeros). Recomputed on save when the glyph or kerning tables change size, keeping the alignment of the file read |
| bdata_ptr | **bitmap** | 16..? | [EacImage](#eacimage) | Font atlas bitmap data |
| ? | **remaining_bytes** | remaining bytes | Bytes | Unknown purpose |
### **GlyphDefinition** ###
#### **Size**: 11..17 bytes ####
#### **Description**: Glyph definition.<br/>- for FNT version < 200 has length 11 bytes.<br/>- for versions >= 200 and <= 309 - 12 bytes, last byte is padding.<br/>- for versions > 309 - 12th byte is num_kern.<br/>- for versions >= 321 it may be 16 bytes if "format" flag is set to 16-bytes ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **code** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Code of symbol |
| 2 | **width** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Width of symbol in font bitmap |
| 3 | **height** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Height of symbol in font bitmap |
| 4 | **x** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Position (x) of symbol in font bitmap |
| 6 | **y** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Position (y) of symbol in font bitmap |
| 8 | **advance** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Distance from the start of this symbol to the start of the next one in rendered text. 0 in every game font with 16-byte glyphs, which keep it in `x_advance` |
| 9 | **x_offset** | 1 | 1-byte signed integer | Offset (x) for drawing the character image |
| 10 | **y_offset** | 1 | 1-byte signed integer | Offset (y) for drawing the character image |
| 11 | **num_kern** | 0..1 | Optional (if ^^version > 309): 1-byte unsigned integer | Number of kerning pairs with this glyph as the right (second) glyph |
| 11..12 | **pad** | 0..1 | Optional (if ^^version <= 309): 1-byte unsigned integer | Padding |
| 11..13 | **kern_index** | 0..2 | Optional (if ^^flags/format == 16-bytes): 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Index of the first kerning pair with this glyph as the right glyph: its `num_kern` pairs follow each other in the kerning table from here. 0 if the glyph has no kerning pairs |
| 11..15 | **x_advance** | 0..2 | Optional (if ^^flags/format == 16-bytes): 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Distance from the start of this symbol to the start of the next one in rendered text, for 16-byte glyphs (`advance` is 0 in all of them in the game files) |
### **KerningItem** ###
#### **Size**: 4 bytes ####
#### **Description**: Kerning pair: horizontal adjustment of the gap between two specific glyphs ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **left** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Code of left glyph |
| 2 | **kerning** | 1 | 1-byte signed integer | Kerning amount in pixels, added to the gap between the glyphs |
| 3 | **right** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Code of right glyph |
## **Audio** ##
### **EaAudioStreams** ###
#### **Size**: 0..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: A file of EA audio streams (`SCHl`): NFS2 / NFS2 SE `.ASF` (a song), NFS2 / NFS2 SE / NFS3 `.MUS` (interactive music: a stream per node of the `.MAP` file of the same name), NFS4 `Data/Audio/MUSIC/*.ASF`, NFS5 songs in `GameData/Music/zzzymus.viv`, NFS6 `audio/music/*.asf`, NFS6 speech in `radio.viv`. Converted to WAV with FFmpeg: a file with one stream to `<name>.wav` + `<name>.meta.json` (loop), a file with more streams to a folder with `<index>.wav` + `<index>.meta.json` per stream and `playthrough.wav` (the streams in the order of the `.LIN`, else `.MAP` file next to it, see `EaMusicMap`; all streams in file order without one) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **streams** | streams up to the end of file\*12..? | Array of `streams up to the end of file` items<br/>Item type: [EaAudioStream](#eaaudiostream) | Audio streams |
### **EaAudioStream** ###
#### **Size**: 12..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: EA audio stream (NFS2 - NFS6 music, NFS6 speech): header chunk "SCHl" with a sound patch (sampling rate, channels, number of samples, loop, codec), then the wave data in chunks of 8-byte header (id, length including the header) and data: SCCl (amount of SCDl chunks), SCDl (wave data), SCLl (loop end), SCEl (end). Explained by [vgmstream](https://github.com/vgmstream/vgmstream) (`ea_schl.c`); the converter decodes it with FFmpeg ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 4 | UTF-8 string. Always == "SCHl" | Header chunk id |
| 4 | **header_length** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Length of the header chunk, including the chunk id and this field |
| 8 | **header** | 4..? | [EaSoundPatch](#easoundpatch) | Sound patch: tags before `info_start` are playback settings, the ones after it describe the wave data. Without the `version` tag (NFS2 - NFS4) `codec` 7 is EA-XA ADPCM v1, no `codec` is 16-bit little endian PCM (NFS3 menu music: each SCDl chunk holds the amount of samples, 4 bytes, then the samples, channels interleaved), the sampling rate is 22050 without `sampling_rate`; with `version` 1 (NFS5, NFS6) the codec is EA-XA ADPCM v2 ("R1" in FFmpeg). `loop_start` / `loop_end` are sample indices of the loop |
| 12..? | **header_padding** | header_length - (header fields length) | Bytes | Zeros up to the end of the header chunk |
| 12 + header_length - (header fields length)..? | **data** | chunks up to and including the end chunk SCEl | Bytes | Chunks SCCl, SCDl, SCLl, SCEl with the wave data, as they are in the file |
| 12 + header_length - (header fields length) + chunks up to and including the end chunk SCEl..? | **padding** | up to the next stream or the end of file | Bytes | Zeros aligning the next stream of the file to 4 bytes |
### **EaSoundPatch** ###
#### **Size**: 4..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: EA sound patch ("PT" header): a sound of a BNKl sound bank as a list of tags. Tags before `info_start` are playback settings (priority, volume, pan, pitch bend range...), tags after it describe the wave data: `num_samples`, `channels` (default 1), `sampling_rate` (default 22050), loop sample indices `loop_start` and `loop_end` (inclusive; a sample loops when it has one of them, from 0 / up to the last sample when the other one is missing), `data_offset` (wave data offset from the start of the bank file) and the codec. Without the `version` tag, `codec` 7 is EA-XA ADPCM v1, 9 is EA MicroTalk 10:1 (speech), no `codec` tag is 16-bit little endian PCM. With `version` 1, `codec_2` 8 is 16-bit little endian PCM, 9 is signed 8-bit PCM, no `codec_2` tag is EA-XA ADPCM v2. Stereo samples are interleaved. A sound can have several layers, played together, separated by the `layer_end` tag, each one with its own settings and wave data (NFS3 player car engines add a short mono loop to the stereo engine sample) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **platform_magic** | 2 | UTF-8 string. Always == "PT" | Patch header magic |
| 2 | **platform** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Platform id, 0 is PC |
| 4 | **tags** | up to and including tag "end"..? | Array of `up to and including tag "end"` items<br/>Item type: [EaSoundPatchTag](#easoundpatchtag) | Tags |
### **EaSoundPatchTag** ###
#### **Size**: 1..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: A tag of EA sound patch: tag id, then (except for tags 0xFC-0xFF) the length of the value and the value, big endian unsigned. Tag meanings follow [vgmstream](https://github.com/vgmstream/vgmstream) (`ea_schl.c`), the ones named `unk_*` are not known ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **tag** | 1 | Enum of 256 possible values<br/><details><summary>Value names:</summary>0 (0x0): unk_0x00<br/>6 (0x6): priority<br/>7 (0x7): unk_0x07<br/>8 (0x8): release_envelope<br/>9 (0x9): playback_envelope<br/>10 (0xa): bend_range_semitones<br/>11 (0xb): bank_channels<br/>12 (0xc): pan<br/>13 (0xd): random_pan_range<br/>14 (0xe): volume<br/>15 (0xf): random_volume_range<br/>16 (0x10): detune<br/>17 (0x11): random_detune_range<br/>18 (0x12): unk_0x12<br/>19 (0x13): effect_bus<br/>20 (0x14): user_data<br/>128 (0x80): version<br/>130 (0x82): channels<br/>131 (0x83): codec<br/>132 (0x84): sampling_rate<br/>133 (0x85): num_samples<br/>134 (0x86): loop_start<br/>135 (0x87): loop_end<br/>136 (0x88): data_offset<br/>137 (0x89): data_offset_channel_2<br/>138 (0x8a): unk_0x8a<br/>139 (0x8b): unk_0x8b<br/>140 (0x8c): flags<br/>145 (0x91): unk_0x91<br/>146 (0x92): unk_0x92<br/>147 (0x93): unk_0x93<br/>160 (0xa0): codec_2<br/>252 (0xfc): padding<br/>253 (0xfd): info_start<br/>254 (0xfe): layer_end<br/>255 (0xff): end</details> | Tag id |
| 1 | **value_length** | 0..1 | Optional (if tag is not padding, info_start, layer_end or end): 1-byte unsigned integer | Length of value in bytes. 0 means value 0 |
| 1..2 | **value** | 0..value_length | Optional (if tag is not padding, info_start, layer_end or end): Bytes | Value, big endian unsigned integer |
